## Question 1: LED Resistors 🛡️ {.quiz-question .smaller}

Why is it **mandatory** to place a resistor in series with an LED when connecting it to power?

- [To convert the power from Alternating Current (AC) to Direct Current (DC).]{data-explanation="Incorrect. A resistor only opposes current flow; it does not convert electrical formats."}
- [To limit the electrical current so the LED doesn't burn out.]{.correct data-explanation="Exactly! LEDs have very little resistance. Without a resistor, they draw too much current and burn out almost instantly."}
- [To store electrical energy like a tiny battery.]{data-explanation="No, that is a capacitor's job. Resistors do not store energy; they dissipate excess voltage as heat."}
- [To change the color of the LED's light.]{data-explanation="No. LED color is determined by the physical semiconductor materials, not the resistor value."}

## Question 2: Wokwi Debugging 🔌 {.quiz-question .smaller}

We wired up a traffic light LED to **Pin 13** in Wokwi, but when we run this code, the LED stays completely **OFF** in the simulation:

```cpp
void setup() {
  // Setup runs once
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(13, HIGH); // Turn LED on
}
```

Why is the LED not turning on?

- [We used HIGH instead of ON or 1 which causes a compilation crash.]{data-explanation="No! HIGH is the standard Arduino keyword representing 5V/logic 1."}
- [Arduino pins can only be turned on by using analogWrite(13, 255);.]{data-explanation="No! digitalWrite works perfectly for turning an output pin ON, provided it has been initialized."}
- [Wokwi doesn't support Pin 13 because it is reserved for the USB programmer.]{data-explanation="Incorrect! Pin 13 is a standard GPIO pin and is fully simulated in Wokwi (it even connects to the built-in 'L' LED)."}
- [We forgot to configure Pin 13 as an output in setup using `pinMode(13, OUTPUT);`.]{.correct data-explanation="Brilliant! Arduino pins default to INPUT mode for safety. If you don't configure the pin as an OUTPUT, it acts as a high-impedance listener and cannot supply enough current to light the LED."}

## Question 3: Heavy DC Motors ⚙️ {.quiz-question .smaller}

Why can't we connect our heavy DC drive motors **directly** to the Arduino's digital output pins?

- [Motors draw far more current than the Arduino pins can supply, which would destroy the chip.]{.correct data-explanation="Spot on! Arduino pins can safely output about 20-40 mA. DC motors can draw hundreds of milliamps (or more when stalled), so we must use an H-bridge driver circuit as a power mediator."}
- [Because DC motors only run on alternating current (AC) power.]{data-explanation="No, these are DC motors and run perfectly on Direct Current (DC)."}
- [Arduino pins can only output 0V, never 5V.]{data-explanation="Incorrect. Arduino digital pins output 5V in HIGH state, which is the correct voltage, but they lack the current capacity."}
- [The motor will spin backwards if connected directly.]{data-explanation="No, spin direction depends on polarity, but the direct connection will burn the pin before the motor spins reliably anyway."}

## Question 4: Actuation & Speeds 🚗 {.quiz-question .smaller}

We want our 4WD smart car to drive forward at a **medium speed** (roughly half power). Which Arduino command should we use?

- [`digitalWrite(ML_PWM, HIGH);`]{data-explanation="No! digitalWrite only outputs fully ON (5V/255 speed) or fully OFF (0V/0 speed)."}
- [`analogWrite(ML_PWM, 127);`]{.correct data-explanation="Correct! analogWrite uses Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) from 0 to 255. A value of 127 is roughly 50% speed!"}
- [`analogWrite(ML_PWM, 50);`]{data-explanation="Not quite. While this controls speed, 50 out of 255 is only ~20% power, which is too low to reliably turn the motors."}
- [`analogRead(ML_PWM);`]{data-explanation="No! analogRead is used to READ signals from sensors, not to send power outputs to motors."}

## Question 5: Servo Wiring Colors 🌈 {.quiz-question .smaller}

When wiring your **SG90 Servo Motor** to the Keyestudio Sensor Shield, which wire color corresponds to **Ground (GND)**?

- [Red]{data-explanation="Danger! Red is VCC/Power (5V). Connecting power to GND or Signal pins can destroy your sensor or servo."}
- [Brown or Black]{.correct data-explanation="Perfect! Standard SG90 servo wiring uses Brown (or Black) for Ground, Red for Power (VCC), and Orange (or Yellow) for the Signal."}
- [Orange or Yellow]{data-explanation="Incorrect. Orange or Yellow is the PWM control Signal line, not Ground."}
- [Green]{data-explanation="No. Standard SG90 servos do not have a green wire."}

## Question 6: Sensor Math 🦇 {.quiz-question .smaller}

When calculating distance using the Ultrasonic Sensor, our code divides the Echo duration by **2** (`distance = duration * 0.034 / 2`). Why do we do this?

- [To account for the two sensor cylinders (Trig and Echo)]{data-explanation="No! The number of cylinders doesn't change the speed of sound or travel physics."}
- [The sound wave travels to the object AND back, so we divide by 2 to get the one-way distance.]{.correct data-explanation="Spot on! The sensor measures the total round-trip time. We only want the distance from the robot to the wall, which is half of the total trip."}
- [To convert the speed of sound from meters to centimeters]{data-explanation="Incorrect. The multiplication by 0.034 (speed of sound in cm/µs) handles the unit conversion, not the division by 2."}
- [Because Arduino runs at 5V but the sensor runs at 2.5V]{data-explanation="No! The sensor runs at 5V and this has absolutely nothing to do with voltage."}

## Question 7: Sweeping the Radar 🧹 {.quiz-question .smaller}

We want to sweep our servo motor smoothly from **0° to 180°** in 1-degree increments, waiting 15ms at each step. Which Arduino code structure is correct?

- [`for (int pos = 0; pos <= 180; pos += 1) { myServo.write(pos); delay(15); }`]{.correct data-explanation="Perfect! The for-loop increments the 'pos' variable, writes it to the servo, and waits for it to physically arrive."}
- [`if (pos <= 180) { myServo.write(pos); delay(15); }`]{data-explanation="No. An 'if' statement only runs once per loop execution. It will not sweep smoothly in a single action."}
- [`myServo.write(0); delay(15); myServo.write(180);`]{data-explanation="No! This will make the servo jump violently from 0 to 180 directly, rather than sweeping smoothly."}
- [`while (pos == 180) { myServo.write(pos); }`]{data-explanation="No. This creates an infinite loop or won't run at all because pos must start at 0 and move up."}

## Question 8: Tank Steering Turn 🔄 {.quiz-question .smaller}

To perform a sharp **tank turn to the LEFT** in place, how should the left and right motors spin?

- [Left motor FORWARD and Right motor BACKWARD.]{data-explanation="No, that would steer the car to the RIGHT, not the left."}
- [Both motors FORWARD, but the left motor at a slower speed.]{data-explanation="No, that is a sweeping turn, not a sharp 'tank turn' in place."}
- [Both motors BACKWARD.]{data-explanation="Incorrect. That will make the car drive straight backwards."}
- [Left motor BACKWARD and Right motor FORWARD.]{.correct data-explanation="Exactly! By spinning the left wheels backward (ML_Ctrl = LOW) and the right wheels forward (MR_Ctrl = HIGH), the car spins quickly on its center axis."}

## Question 9: Autonomous Logic ⚖️ {.quiz-question .smaller}

Look at this decision block. When will the robot decide to **stop and reverse**?

```cpp
int distance = measureDistance();
if (distance < 20 && distance > 2) {
  stopAndReverse();
} else {
  driveForward();
}
```

- [When the distance is between 2 cm and 20 cm.]{.correct data-explanation="Exactly! The '&&' operator means BOTH conditions must be true: the object must be closer than 20cm, but greater than 2cm (to ignore error/0 readings)."}
- [Only when the distance is exactly 20 cm or exactly 2 cm.]{data-explanation="No, '<' and '>' represent ranges (less than and greater than), not exact equality ('==')."}
- [When the distance is either less than 20 cm OR greater than 2 cm.]{data-explanation="No! That would be the '||' (OR) operator. The '&&' (AND) operator requires both to be true."}
- [When there are no obstacles in front.]{data-explanation="Incorrect! When the distance is large (e.g. 50cm), it goes to the 'else' block and drives forward."}

## Question 10: The Backwards Escape 🔙 {.quiz-question .smaller}

Our robot gets stuck in a narrow corner where both `distLeft` and `distRight` are smaller than 10 cm. Which conditional check correctly detects this double-stuck condition to trigger a reverse escape?

- [`if (distLeft < 10 && distRight < 10) { car_back(); }`]{.correct data-explanation="Spot on! The '&&' (AND) operator ensures the reverse action is triggered only when BOTH the left AND right sides are blocked."}
- [`if (distLeft < 10 || distRight < 10) { car_back(); }`]{data-explanation="No! The '||' (OR) operator would make the robot reverse if *either* side is blocked, which makes it back up too early even if one side is completely open."}
- [`if (distLeft < 10 + distRight < 10) { car_back(); }`]{data-explanation="No, the '+' operator performs addition, which is invalid syntax here for logical checks."}
- [`if (distLeft == distRight) { car_back(); }`]{data-explanation="No, this only checks if the distances are exactly equal, not if they are blocked."}

## Question 11: Rover Integration 🛰️ {.quiz-question .smaller}

In the **"Smart Remote" Rover challenge**, our robot receives an IR remote command to drive **FORWARD**, but the ultrasonic sensor detects a wall just **10 cm** away. What is the correct priority logic?

- [The remote is king! Ignore the sensor and drive forward.]{data-explanation="Danger! This will crash your robot directly into the wall, causing physical damage."}
- [Ignore the remote's 'FORWARD' button, stop the motors, but still allow 'BACKWARD' or 'TURN' commands.]{.correct data-explanation="Brilliant! Safety override! You block dangerous commands (Forward) but keep the robot responsive so the driver can back away or steer clear."}
- [Shutdown the entire Arduino board automatically.]{data-explanation="No, shutting down means the robot becomes completely unresponsive and you cannot control it anymore."}
- [Drive forward anyway, but sound a beep sound.]{data-explanation="No, a beep doesn't stop the physical impact. Safety must be absolute."}
